## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-06-02
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)
**System Name:** Guest Cottage

## SYSTEM STATUS
This maintenance visit recorded several findings requiring attention. The primary tank scum layer is elevated, the effluent filter shows moderate soiling, and dissolved oxygen was not measured on an aerobic treatment unit. These factors together indicate that treatment effectiveness cannot be fully assessed at this time. The dispersal field is performing normally.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 5.5 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 44 in |
| Sludge Depth | Not measured during this maintenance visit |

**Solids Content:** Cannot be calculated. Sludge depth was not measured; the sludge judge was not available on this visit. Without both scum and sludge measurements, total solids content cannot be determined, and pumping need cannot be assessed.

## EFFLUENT FILTER
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Filter Condition | Fair |
| Soiling Level | Moderate |
| Action Taken | Cleaned and reseated |

The filter was cleaned during this maintenance visit. Moderate soiling indicates biological load is present in the tank and the filter is performing its intended function of trapping solids before discharge.

## PUMP PERFORMANCE
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Amp Draw | 3.1 A |
| High Water Alarm | Functional |

The pump is drawing current and the high water alarm is operational. Nameplate full-load amps for this pump are not recorded in the equipment file, so the amp draw cannot be compared to the manufacturer's specification. The reading of 3.1 A is within the typical range for a 0.5 horsepower 115-volt pump, but without nameplate data, this assessment is indicative only.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
The dispersal field surface is dry with no ponding or wet areas observed during the maintenance visit. The field is accepting effluent normally.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum thickness and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump and recorded amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and assessed surface condition

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**Priority 1 -- Treatment Assessment**
Dissolved oxygen was not measured during this maintenance visit. This is an aerobic treatment unit, and dissolved oxygen is the primary indicator of treatment effectiveness. The regulatory minimum is 2 mg/L; readings below 1 mg/L indicate anaerobic conditions and probable treatment failure. Recommend measuring dissolved oxygen at the next maintenance visit to establish current treatment status.

**Priority 2 -- Solids Accumulation**
Sludge depth was not measured during this maintenance visit. The scum layer measured 5.5 inches, which is elevated. Combined with moderate filter soiling, this suggests biological load is accumulating in the tank. At the next maintenance visit, measure sludge depth so that total solids content can be calculated and pumping need can be determined. If solids content exceeds 33 percent of tank volume, pumping is recommended.

**Priority 3 -- Equipment File**
Nameplate full-load amps for the effluent pump are not recorded in the equipment file. Obtain this specification from the pump nameplate or manufacturer documentation and add it to the file. This will allow future amp draw readings to be compared against the correct standard.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### About the Scum Layer
This maintenance visit recorded a scum layer of 5.5 inches. Scum is the layer of grease, oils and light solids that floats on the surface of the tank. A scum layer of 4 to 5 inches is typical; above that, it may indicate that grease or inappropriate products are entering the system more heavily than usual. Avoid pouring cooking grease down the drain, and do not flush wipes, paper towels, or other non-biodegradable material. These materials do not break down in the tank and accumulate as scum.

### About the Aerobic Treatment Unit
Your system includes an aerobic treatment unit, which means it uses air and beneficial bacteria to break down waste more completely than a conventional septic tank alone. This process is more effective but also more sensitive to what enters the system. Harsh chemicals, antibacterial soaps, and bleach can harm the bacteria that do the treatment work. Use these products sparingly and in normal household amounts.

### Next Maintenance Visit
The next routine maintenance visit is due in 12 months. At that visit, sludge depth will be measured and dissolved oxygen will be tested so that treatment performance can be fully assessed.
